entrypoints.summary: A local caller creates maps and loads a BPF_PROG_TYPE_SOCKET_FILTER through BPF_MAP_CREATE and BPF_PROG_LOAD, then attaches and executes it through a socket pair.

negative_controls: No observed run output is included in the bundle.
The organizer warns that the challenge weakens speculative-execution mitigation, limiting transfer to unmodified kernels.
observability.positive_marker: The exploit source prints a success message and invokes a shell after overwrite_cred returns successfully.

preconditions: Local ability to invoke eBPF map and program-load syscalls in the provided challenge runtime.
The custom challenge kernel includes the vulnerable ROL implementation and weakened speculative-execution branch exploration described by the organizer.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: Crafted BPF instruction sequence containing branch-refined scalar arithmetic and ROL, followed by map-pointer arithmetic.
trigger_steps.summary: Create maps, load a socket-filter eBPF program, attach it, and trigger execution by writing to the paired socket.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: Map offsets selected from the verifier/runtime range confusion and map-field corruption used to establish arbitrary read/write.
trigger_steps.summary: Use out-of-bounds map-relative accesses to obtain leaks and corrupt map metadata, then overwrite the credential pointer with init_cred.

capabilities.concept: arbitrary kernel memory read and write

mitigations.concept: conservative rotate-left abstract interpretation with preserved pointer-ALU sanitization

relation_candidates.rationale: The attacker can submit an eBPF program containing the added ROL instruction and branch-refined scalar state to the verifier.
The erroneous modeled offset is accepted for map pointer arithmetic while the concrete rotated offset accesses outside the permitted map-relative region.

relation_candidates.dst: arbitrary kernel memory read and write
relation_candidates.rationale: The writeup describes using out-of-bounds accesses to leak pointers and corrupt bpf_map fields, which are then used for arbitrary read and write.
The described arbitrary write replaces the current task credential pointer with init_cred.
relation_candidates.src: arbitrary kernel memory read and write

relation_candidates.dst: conservative rotate-left abstract interpretation with preserved pointer-ALU sanitization
relation_candidates.rationale: A conservative ROL transfer function and retained pointer-ALU sanitization prevent acceptance of concrete offsets excluded by verifier state.

impact.affected_asset: Kernel memory integrity and current process credential state.
impact.attacker_capability: A local actor able to load and execute the crafted eBPF program can derive kernel information leaks, arbitrary kernel read/write primitives, and replace its credential pointer with init_cred.
impact.security_effect: Local kernel privilege escalation in the supplied challenge environment.

causal_trace.summary: The challenge patch adds immediate 32- and 64-bit BPF ROL operations to the runtime interpreter and admits them to verifier scalar processing.

The verifier derives post-ROL scalar extrema by rotating the separately tracked minimum and maximum values, while runtime rotates the concrete register value; a branch-refined interval can therefore exclude the concrete post-rotation value.

A BPF map pointer is adjusted using the verifier-accepted but concretely different scalar offset, permitting map-relative out-of-bounds accesses that leak map/kernel pointers and corrupt bpf_map fields.

The described chain constructs arbitrary read and write, finds the current task credential pointer, and overwrites it with init_cred; the supplied exploit source reports success and starts a shell after credential overwrite.

failure.operation: Verifier approval of map-pointer arithmetic whose runtime scalar offset is outside the modeled range, followed by out-of-bounds map-relative reads and writes.

primary_invariant.statement: For every scalar value reachable at runtime after a ROL instruction, the verifier's tracked bounds and tnum must conservatively include that value before it is used in pointer arithmetic.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The added ROL transfer functions rotate stored extrema independently and shift the tnum rather than conservatively representing rotation of all values in the pre-operation abstract set.

quality.review_notes: Primary challenge patch and organizer writeup support the mechanism. The supplied material contains exploit source and a QEMU launcher but no captured execution result, so reproducibility is not asserted. The organizer states that speculative-execution branch exploration was weakened for this challenge and that this route is not a complete bypass in an unmodified real-world verifier configuration. The supplied kernel patch is the vulnerable challenge change, not a remediation patch.

remediation.invariant_restored: ROL analysis must over-approximate all concrete rotated scalar values used as pointer offsets, and pointer arithmetic must remain subject to its sanitizer checks.
mitigation_classes: sound abstract-domain transfer function for bit rotation
conservative scalar-bound and tnum invalidation when rotate cannot be represented precisely
preserve pointer-ALU sanitization and speculative-path checks

state_context.attacker_state_setup: The writeup sets a map value to zero from userspace, derives an uncertain verifier range with an AND and branch, then rotates it so concrete and modeled values diverge; the BPF loader creates and executes socket-filter programs.
data_structure_invariants: Verifier scalar bounds and tnum must conservatively cover runtime scalar values.
Map-relative pointer offsets accepted by the verifier must remain in bounds at runtime.
The bpf_map fields used for map operations must not be reachable for attacker-directed corruption through map data access.

numeric_domains.attacker_constraints: The illustrated sequence produces a verifier range of 3 through 7 with concrete value 4 before a rotate-left by 62; the writeup states the concrete result becomes 1 while tracked extrema diverge.
numeric_domains.name: eBPF scalar after branch and ROL

state_context.state_machine: A user-controlled map value is loaded into an eBPF scalar, constrained by arithmetic and a branch, transformed by ROL, and then consumed in map-pointer arithmetic under verifier analysis before runtime execution.

target.component: custom eBPF ROL interpreter and verifier scalar-range tracking
